body:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

We're looking for a Research Engineer to help make Claude more capable, reliable and useful on complex, real-world work. You'll work across research and engineering, from early ideas and experiments through to improvements in our models.

This is an early-stage team working on open-ended problems. Priorities will change as we learn, and you'll have a lot of ownership over what you work on. We're looking for someone who's excited about that, and who enjoys working closely with both research and product.

Key responsibilities

•
Design and run experiments to improve model capabilities

•
Build reinforcement learning environments and evaluations

•
Develop the tools and infrastructure needed to support this research

•
Collaborate with teams across research, engineering and product

•
Help shape the direction of a new area of research

Minimum qualifications

•
Strong software engineering skills, including proficiency in Python

•
Experience training, fine-tuning or evaluating machine learning models

•
A track record of owning ambiguous technical projects end to end

•
Strong communication skills and a collaborative working style

•
Care about the societal impacts and safety of your work

Preferred qualifications

•
Experience with reinforcement learning, particularly in long-horizon or sparse-reward settings

•
Experience building reinforcement learning environments, simulation systems or large-scale ML infrastructure

•
Experience building evaluations or benchmarks for agentic systems

•
Experience working closely with product teams to drive model improvements

Representative projects

•
Build a simulation where decisions made early on have consequences much later, and use it to train a model

•
Design an evaluation for work that takes a long time and has no single right answer

•
Investigate where a model's independence breaks down on long projects, and run experiments to improve it

•
Develop a way for people to oversee a large amount of work without reviewing every step

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$500,000 — $850,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Every time Anthropic releases a model, we publish a system card: a long-form technical document that describes the model's capabilities, safety properties, evaluation results, and the reasoning behind our deployment decisions. System cards are some of the most consequential and widely read documents we produce, and they are one way we hold ourselves publicly accountable for the safety claims we make.

We're hiring a Research Operations Specialist to help own system card production. You'll work embedded with research and safety teams through each launch, coordinating contributions from dozens of researchers, holding the schedule and the open-threads list, and making sure the document ships on time as a single, accurate, internally consistent whole. Along the way you'll do real editorial work: turning results and researcher notes into clear, honest prose and pushing back when an explanation doesn't hold together.

System cards sit within a wider family of external safety artifacts, including risk reports and Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) updates. Part of this role is keeping the system card consistent with those documents so that Anthropic's public safety story reads as one coherent account rather than several.

This role sits in Research Operations and works closely with Alignment, Safeguards, Frontier Red Team, and capabilities research. The core of the job is part project management, part translation: keeping a complex, many-author, hard-deadline document on track while making frontier safety research legible to researchers, policymakers, journalists, and the public — without sacrificing precision.

Key responsibilities

• Coordinate dozens of contributors across Alignment, Safeguards, Frontier Red Team, Interpretability, and capabilities research; chase drafts, resolve differences of perspective, seek ground truth, and run final formatting and polish

• Edit, and sometimes write, content; work directly with researchers to turn their results, notes, and plots into clear, scientific, non-marketing prose and maintain Anthropic's voice across sections drafted by many different people

• Guard accuracy and consistency; catch terminology drift, claims that subtly contradict each other, and discrepancies between internal communications and system card drafts

• Keep the system card aligned with related artifacts; track what's being said in risk reports, RSP disclosures, and other safety documentation so the system card stays consistent with them, and flag conflicts early

• Improve the process between launches; build and maintain templates, style guidance, contributor guides, checklists, and reusable section scaffolds so each cycle starts from a stronger baseline

• Pick up other research-adjacent operations and writing, such as internal research summaries, release notes, and documentation that helps research leadership communicate clearly

Minimum qualifications

• Strong project management and execution skills; able to track dozens of open threads to closure during compressed launch periods with many moving parts and many owners

• Demonstrated ability to coordinate and influence without direct authority, building trust while chasing drafts and giving constructive editorial feedback

• Excellent technical writing skills; able to take dense, jargon-heavy source material and produce prose that is precise, honest, and readable by a non-specialist

• Comfort working closely with researchers; able to read an evaluation results table, ask the right clarifying questions, and push back when an explanation doesn't hold together

• Working knowledge of large language models (LLMs) at a conceptual level, including fluency with vocabulary such as pretraining, reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), context windows, evals, and red-teaming

• Data communication literacy; able to identify how a chart or table could be made clearer and more accurate

• High integrity and a genuine sense of accountability around producing documents that hold Anthropic publicly responsible for its safety claims

Preferred qualifications

• Familiarity with AI safety, AI policy, alignment research, evaluation methodology, or the RSP landscape beyond baseline LLM knowledge

• Background in science communication, research publishing, or technical journalism

• A track record of shipping long-form technical documents, such as research reports, whitepapers, technical standards, regulatory filings, or science journalism

• Experience with safety, risk, or compliance documentation, such as regulatory submissions, safety cases, security disclosures, or clinical or scientific reporting

• Skill in visual communication and experience shipping polished, on-brand documents

• Light scripting or tooling ability (enough to automate a formatting check or wrangle a spreadsheet)

body:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

Anthropic manages one of the industry's largest AI fleets — spanning multiple accelerator families, cpu families and clouds. The Capacity Engineering team is responsible for making sure all our infrastructure resources are accounted for, well-utilized, and efficiently allocated. We own the data, tooling, and operational systems that let Anthropic plan, measure, and maximize utilization across first-party and third-party compute.

As an engineer on Capacity Engineering, you will build the production systems that power this work: data pipelines that ingest and normalize telemetry from heterogeneous cloud environments, observability tooling that gives the org real-time visibility into fleet health, and performance instrumentation that measures how efficiently every major workload uses the hardware it’s running on. You will be expected to write production-quality code every day, operate alongside Kubernetes-native infrastructure at meaningful scale, and directly influence decisions around Capacity.

You’ll collaborate closely with research engineering, infrastructure, inference, and finance teams. The work requires someone who can move between data engineering, systems engineering, and observability with comfort — and who thrives in a high-autonomy, high-ambiguity environment.

This is a pipeline role feeding four areas. Depending on your background and business priority, you’ll focus primarily in one, but the boundaries are fluid and the problems overlap:

• Data platform Pipelines that ingest occupancy and utilization telemetry from Kubernetes clusters, normalize billing and usage across cloud providers, and serve the BigQuery tables the rest of the org queries against. Correctness, completeness, and latency are the job, not a footnote. Consumers range from research engineers to finance to leadership, so it's product work as much as engineering: defining schema contracts, making data discoverable, and figuring out what people actually need.

• Planning Knowing what the fleet has, where it's going, and what's in the way. Making the state of the fleet legible and actionable in real time: cluster health tooling, capacity planning platforms, alerting on occupancy drops and allocation problems, and systemic fixes to scheduling and fragmentation. Kubernetes operations on one side, cross-team coordination on the other.

• Efficiency Measuring and improving how effectively every major workload uses the hardware it runs on. Instrumenting utilization across training, inference, and eval systems, building benchmarking infrastructure, establishing per-config baselines, and working directly with system-owning teams to close the gaps. The metric has to be good enough that the team on the hook for it agrees with the number.

• Attribution and forecasting Connecting what the fleet costs to what the business is doing with it. Reconciling CSP billing exports against vendor telemetry and internal systems with mismatched schemas, attributing spend to the workloads and teams that generate it, and turning inference demand signals and research roadmaps into a defensible compute plan. Efficiency metrics have to survive contact with finance: stripped of pure demand and unit-price effects, reproducible month over month, and legible to a CFO.

Key responsibilities

• Build the planning and allocation stack — the tools leadership uses to allocate capacity, teams use to plan against their allocations, and the scheduler enforces. Cross-region and cross-provider placement, guardrails, queueing, occupancy KPIs.

• Drive the efficiency programs: stranding and rightsizing, unused capacity recovery, and job-level utilization across training, inference, and eval. Establish per-config baselines and work with system-owning teams to close the gaps. Directly influence decisions around a significant area of company investment.

• Own attribution and forecasting — reconcile billing across ten-plus providers against telemetry and internal systems, attribute spend to the workloads that generate it, and turn demand signals and research roadmaps into a defensible compute plan and supply pipeline.

• Build the data platform underneath all of it: pipelines ingesting occupancy, utilization, and cost from a rapidly diversifying fleet into BigQuery, with real ownership of completeness, latency SLOs, and gap detection. Every new provider is a net-new integration.

body:
🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts , accounts for 16-17 year olds , a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save , invest and combine their pensions with us.

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not only about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo.

📍London/Cardiff/UK Remote | 💰£85,000 - £115,000 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance + Benefits ✨

⭐️ Our Third Party & Outsourcing Risk Management Team

We are a high-performing Global team focused on delivering pragmatic Third Party Risk Management (‘TPRM’) that protects Monzo and our customers globally. As Monzo expands across new markets and scales its product range, the operational footprint is growing fast, and the operating environment is becoming more complex.

We’re looking for a Senior Third Party Risk Manager to help shape and deliver our approach. As well as ensuring Monzo’s TPRM has well defined controls, processes and governance models in place to meet the continually growing and evolving demands of global Third Party Risk Management regulations - you’ll also set priorities and turn them into measurable improvements.

Reporting to the Director of Third Party Risk, this is a hands-on role, with strategic scope. You’ll work across the global team, and with a variety of stakeholders throughout Monzo, to strengthen our framework, manage complex risks and improve how we deliver TPRM both tactically and strategically.

🔑 You’ll play a key role by...

• Delivering Core TPRM Operations Globally : Operating end-to-end operational activities, including supplier tiering, materiality assessments, due diligence reviews, exit planning support, and regulatory reporting.

• Driving Operational Excellence: Taking ownership of process quality, making sure TPRM activities are completed accurately, consistently and on time. You’ll look for ways to improve how we manage third party risk in practice.

• Helping shape our priorities: Identifying emerging risks, gaps and opportunities across third party risk management, and making recommendations to inform the team’s strategy and roadmap. You’ll develop practical solutions and help deliver improvements through to completion.

• Enabling Strategic Delivery: Supporting and feeding into higher-level strategic initiatives and complex risk landscapes. Leading agreed initiatives from problem definition through implementation autonomously, working across teams and global markets to deliver measurable improvements and ensuring clear visibility throughout.

• Collaborating Across Teams: Working directly with internal stakeholders across the 3LOD, and external suppliers to clear blockers, follow up on actions, and resolve issues effectively.

• Sharing your expertise: Support colleagues and stakeholders with practical guidance, helping them understand how to deliver their third party risk responsibilities.

🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…

• You know Outsourcing, Third Party Risk & Regulation: You have substantial practical TPRM experience (ideally in banking or financial services) operating in both the UK and EU financial markets.

• You’ve contributed to a risk strategy, framework or operating model: You can demonstrate how you translated an identified gap into a practical improvement.

• You’re comfortable leading complex assessments: You make balanced, well-reasoned recommendations when information is incomplete or stakeholders have different priorities.

• You have experience working with various technologies : TPR tooling and AI to build innovative solutions and streamline operational workflows.

• You hold a high quality bar: You pay close attention to detail and care about accuracy. You use data and reporting to spot patterns, make evidence-based decisions and improve processes.

• You take ownership: You work independently, take initiative and prioritise your workload in a fast-moving environment. You use sound risk judgement and know when to seek guidance or involve others.

• You focus on outcomes, not just activity: You measure success by what has materially improved whether that's faster turnaround times, clearer risk ownership, or cleaner supplier data.

• You are a clear, pragmatic communicator: You build strong relationships with internal teams, third parties and regulators. You’re comfortable holding colleagues accountable and offering constructive challenges when needed. You bring together input from specialists across Information Security, Data Protection, Legal and Operational Resilience to form a clear view of risk.

• You are comfortable escalating: You use sound judgement to know when to involve your team or manager in emerging issues or concerns, and communicate your priorities and workload clearly and regularly, defaulting to transparency and taking accountability.

🙌 What’s in it for you

💰 £85,000 - £115,000 ➕Incentive Awards tied to your performance.

📍This role can be based in our London office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London)

⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team.

📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.

🏡 We will set you up to work from home; all employees are given Macbooks and for fully remote workers we will provide extra support for your work-from-home setup.

➕ Plus lots more! Read our full list of benefits .

🌈 The application journey has 3 key steps

• Short call with a Monzo Recruiter

• Video-call with the Hiring Manager

• Full-Loop Interviews (1 x Role Specific + 1 x Behavioural)

📆 Please Note : We pause hiring from 14th Dec 2026 - 4th January 2027.

Full Loop interviews will take place in January 2027 🥳Thanks for your patience!

⏳We’ll only close this role once we have enough applications for the next stage. Please submit your application as soon as possible to make sure you don’t miss out.

We have some guidelines on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to ace an application and interview at Monzo. You can read them here.

#LI-REMOTE

#CM-1

Equal opportunities for everyone

Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. You can read more in our blog , 2026 Diversity and Inclusion Report and 2025 Gender Pay Gap Report.

We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.

If you have a preferred name, please use it to apply. We don't need full or birth names at application stage.

Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We're looking for a Research Engineer to make Claude better at the real-world work that matters most to Beneficial Deployments. You'll identify where our models fall short, build the environments and reward signals used to train them, run experiments, and measure whether new capabilities generalize beyond the training data. You'll also work closely with the Beneficial Deployments team, helping shape its roadmap based on where AI capabilities are heading.

Key responsibilities

• Identify capability gaps in our models and turn them into a research agenda

• Own the end-to-end process of creating RL environments, from task sourcing and reward design through training, using both real-world and synthetic data

• Collaborate with domain experts to design data pipelines

• Develop and improve QA frameworks to catch reward hacking and ensure env quality

• Run generalization experiments to measure how data strategy changes improve model capabilities

• Partner with other RL research teams and product teams to align on capability goals

Minimum qualifications

• Have experience with fine-tuning large language models for specific domains or real-world use cases

• Have experience with reinforcement learning, reward design, or training data curation for LLMs

• Have a track record of setting your own direction and delivering on ambiguous, high-stakes work with little oversight, such as by running your own team, research program, or company

• Can turn deep technical understanding into clear strategic recommendations that influence senior, non-technical leaders

• Think rigorously about how quickly AI capabilities are advancing and are ready to plan around the possibility that transformative AI arrives soon

• Find value in reading through datasets to understand them and spot issues

• Have experience training production ML systems

• Have experience designing evals or benchmarks for LLMs

• Have domain expertise in healthcare, global health, or philanthropy

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to support our growing Privacy Engineering team: a high-leverage group responsible for designing and operating the privacy infrastructure that protects user data across our AI systems. You'll have an outsized impact in shaping how Anthropic builds world-class privacy into Claude from the ground up.

This is a role with extraordinary scope and leverage. You'll own a large subset of privacy engineering for Anthropic end-to-end. The work spans privacy-preserving architectures for AI training and inference, foundational data governance and lifecycle systems, and the automated controls that turn complex regulation into engineering reality. You'll lead a team of talented privacy engineers that builds and operates the platform and infra frameworks underpinning Anthropic's privacy and compliance posture. Your job is to scale the team and its charter as Anthropic grows.

Working at the intersection of privacy engineering, AI safety, and distributed systems, your team will solve novel challenges in protecting user data at scale, handling billions of conversations while maintaining model quality and research velocity. If owning the whole problem and having an outsized impact on how a frontier AI lab protects its users sounds compelling, this role might be for you.

Key Responsibilities

•
Build and lead the team: Recruit, develop, and retain a team of exceptional privacy engineers; establish team charter, practices, and priorities as the team matures

•
Drive technical strategy: Partner with technical leads, researchers, and legal to set direction for privacy infrastructure across training, inference, and product surfaces: data governance and policy enforcement, deletion and retention at scale, encryption and key management, audit and access transparency, and ML-based PII detection and redaction.

•
Build foundational privacy infrastructure: Guide the team in building automated data discovery, classification, access controls, audit logging, and lifecycle management systems, plus data governance platforms for tracking lineage, purpose limitation, and retention across distributed AI systems

•
Translate regulation into engineering: Ensure the team turns complex regulatory requirements (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, EU AI Act) into actionable technical implementations and automated compliance controls

•
Lead privacy reviews at scale: Oversee technical privacy reviews and threat modeling for new AI models and features, identifying risks and architecting scalable mitigations

•
Enable privacy by default: Champion privacy engineering toolkits and frameworks that let all engineers build privacy-preserving features by default, and embed privacy controls into Claude's inference systems, interfaces, and data pipelines

•
Communicate and coordinate: Work closely with security, legal, data infrastructure, research, and go-to-market teams; clearly articulate dependencies, risks, and progress to stakeholders, and advocate for privacy as central to our mission of AI safety.

•
Stay technically grounded: Maintain enough technical depth to understand your team's work, provide meaningful guidance, and credibly represent privacy concerns in cross-functional discussions

About You

We're looking for a technical leader who thinks of themselves as a problem-solver and team-builder first. The ideal candidate has:

Required:

•
Significant experience managing engineering teams, including hiring and growing teams through periods of ambiguity and rapid change

•
Deep expertise in privacy engineering principles: privacy by design, data minimization, and purpose limitation

•
Strong technical foundation in data governance and privacy infrastructure (policy enforcement, deletion/retention/lineage systems, encryption key management, audit logging) and the ability to discuss them at a level that earns respect from senior ICs.

•
Strong understanding of privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) and the ability to translate legal requirements into technical solutions

•
Experience with data governance, classification, and lifecycle management systems serving large user bases

•
Ability to balance technical depth with pragmatic decision-making; you know when to dive deep and when to trust your team

•
Strong communication skills: you can translate complex privacy challenges into business terms and vice versa

•
Comfort with end-to-end ownership, including defining practices where industry precedent is thin

Preferred:

•
8+ years of experience managing technical teams

•
Experience growing an engineering team and charter through a period of rapid company scaling.

•
Experience conducting privacy reviews, threat modeling, and risk assessments for production systems

•
Proven track record of designing and implementing privacy infrastructure serving millions of users

•
Experience at companies during periods of hypergrowth where you've scaled privacy alongside the business

•
Exposure to AI/ML infrastructure and the unique privacy demands of large-scale training and inference

About the role

Corporate Network Engineering designs, builds, and operates the networks in Anthropic's offices around the world: campus switching, Wi-Fi, and edge. We think a good office network is no more complicated than its requirements demand, fast and reliable enough that users never think about it, secure by default, and tolerant of failures to enable a lean team to operate a global portfolio of offices.

Anthropic is growing quickly, and our team is small and runs with high autonomy, so we care a great deal about how the work gets done: configuration kept in version control and shipped through review and staged rollouts, problems that happen more than once fixed at the source, and incidents closed only once the cause is fixed. We use Claude heavily in this work and expect you to as well.

We're hiring an experienced network engineer who works this way already: someone who has designed, built, and operated campus networks at scale, wired and wireless, and has also built the code and tooling to run them. As a network engineer here you'll work across all of it: network design and standards, new office buildouts, infrastructure as code, monitoring and incident response, and network security, where Corporate Security and Detection & Response are close partners. This is a hands-on individual contributor role.

Responsibilities

• Design, build, and operate campus networks for offices of every size: switching, Wi-Fi, edge, carrier, and out-of-band connectivity

• Have delivered the network for new offices end to end, with real estate, construction, carriers, and integrators

• Prefer the simplest design that meets the requirement, know what you gave up to get it, and write it down clearly enough for others to build from

• Already use AI tools as a core part of how you work, and know which work to hand to a model and which to keep

• Have served as incident commander for incidents that spanned several teams, or built a team's on-call and incident process

• Have migrated a network between platforms or vendors across live sites

• Buildout infrastructure: MDF/IDF design, structured cabling, power and cooling, carrier diversity

Anthropic is building data center capacity across many sites at once, and for every site we own or lease we have committed to invest significantly in the host community, on terms we can stand behind publicly.
We're looking for someone to own our community benefits program end to end, across an international portfolio of many sites, so that every commitment is tracked, funded, paid on schedule and publicly reported. You'll negotiate the community-benefit terms with developers and other counterparties, from the term sheet through the lease, then manage those developers after signature, run the payouts and publish each site's yearly reports.

Program management

• Own the commitments ledger: every community commitment, budget and payout at every site, and who holds the money

• Track payment schedules and rent recovery against each site's construction milestones, with Finance

• Run payouts: check who receives the money, run select programs, such as the electricity credit, through an outside partner, and publish who got what each year

• Own each site's yearly environmental and jobs reports: get the data from developers and utilities, have an outside firm check it, and publish it

• Track what is committed, signed, funded and paid, and where a deal is stuck

• Keep the terms we sign consistent with our public commitments

• Build and hire the team that runs this function on an ongoing basis

Deals

• Negotiate the community-benefit terms in developer leases and capacity agreements: who funds the community commitment, whether it sits on the developer's books or is recovered through rent, and when payments are made during construction

• Work the term sheets with developers and other counterparties, and partner with our data center deal team so these terms are in every new deal and expansion from the start

• Time each site's community commitments to its schedule: as early as the day after lease execution, and no later than substantial completion

• Build and maintain standard form templates for the community commitments and leases, so each new deal starts from an agreed position

• Know how data center sites come together: site selection, leases with developers, power and local approvals

• Have worked in economic development for a data center operator or other large infrastructure developer, on the company's side of the table

• Are fluent in the financial side: funds, payment schedules, how a cost is recovered through rent, and what sits on whose books

• Write clear term sheets and clear updates for executives

• Are comfortable building a function from scratch, quickly and with ambiguity

• Care about Anthropic's mission and about doing right by the communities that host our infrastructure

That work requires physical infrastructure at significant scale, and building that infrastructure the right way means being a real, long-term partner to the communities where we operate.

We are looking for a Community Engagement Manager in Canada to join our Public Policy team and serve as Anthropic's on-the-ground presence in the communities where our data centres are sited, built, and operated. This role sits where community engagement, government relations and public affairs meet, and you may come from any of them. What matters is that you know how decisions get made in Alberta and can earn trust in a county council chamber, a minister's office or a community hall. Your job is to make Anthropic a trusted, visible, and valued neighbour, from the earliest stages of site selection through construction and long-term operations.

You will be the connective tissue between Anthropic's Policy and Infrastructure teams and the local officials, community organizations, economic development partners, and residents who have a stake in what we build. You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly. Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand.

You will travel regularly within Alberta, up to 50% of the time, and occasionally to other Anthropic data centre markets. We will also consider applicants based in Ottawa who have established professional experience or relationships relevant to Alberta and can spend at least half their time in the province.

•

•
Work with colleagues in Alberta to build a playbook and repeatable processes that scale as Anthropic's infrastructure footprint grows

•
Experience in government relations, public affairs, political or government staff roles, community affairs, economic development, or a closely related field

•

•
A skilled relationship and coalition builder who earns trust with a diverse group of stakeholders, and who maintains relationships through difficult conversations

•
The ability to represent a company credibly in public settings, including town halls, hearings, and press interviews

•
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn a complex operational plan into plain language that a local official or reporter can understand and respond to

•
The ability to work independently, get up to speed quickly on complex policy issues, and manage multiple concurrent engagements across different markets without losing track of any of them

•

•
7+ years of experience in government relations, public affairs, or community engagement, ideally including energy, utility, or large-scale industrial infrastructure projects

•
Experience as political staff or in a senior government role in Alberta, at the municipal, provincial, or federal level

•
Experience on a public affairs campaign that combined stakeholder outreach with earned or paid media

•
Familiarity with land use, zoning, and development permitting processes at the municipal and provincial level

•
Experience managing corporate social responsibility programs

•
Established relationships with economic development, workforce, or civic organizations in the markets this role covers

•
Experience working with real estate, legal, communications, and policy teams at the same time

•
Experience working with Indigenous communities in Canada, including familiarity with consultation processes, Indigenous rights and treaty considerations, or community benefit and partnership agreements

A genuine interest in the communities where you work, not just the projects you are managing

About the role
In this role, you'll lead a team of Account Executives driving the adoption of safe, frontier AI with top enterprises across Korea. This role is critical to Anthropic's APAC expansion.

• Build and lead a high-performing team of Account Executives, providing coaching, mentorship, and guidance to drive team success

• Build strong partnerships across the organization to drive strategic initiatives

• Identify and execute on new market opportunities and use cases for Anthropic's AI solutions across enterprise segments, including Korea's large conglomerates and fast-growing digital-native companies

• Help your team navigate complex enterprise stakeholder ecosystems including executives, IT departments, and procurement offices to build alignment

Preferred qualifications

• 15+ years of enterprise sales experience, preferably driving adoption of SaaS or emerging technologies

• 5+ years of sales leadership experience within the Enterprise segment

• Proven track record of building and leading high-performing sales teams selling into large enterprises, with demonstrated success in coaching and developing AEs

• Experience establishing and scaling sales processes, tools, and methodologies in fast-growing organizations

• Strong technical acumen with ability to enable credible AI conversations

• Track record of successful partnership with technical teams throughout the customer journey

• Deep understanding of enterprise buying cycles, procurement frameworks, and common pain points across industries

• Demonstrated ability to navigate complex, multithreaded sales cycles across diverse stakeholder groups and drive cross-functional initiatives

• Experience managing complex enterprise sales cycles and helping AEs secure strategic deals

• Excellent communication skills and ability to build relationships across all levels, from individual contributors to C-suite executives

• Strategic approach to market analysis combined with tactical excellence in execution

• Passion for AI technology and commitment to its safe, responsible development

• Business-level Korean required; English proficiency strongly preferred

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. 🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts , accounts for 16-17 year olds , a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save , invest and combine their pensions with us.

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not only about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo.

📍 London | 💰 £98,000 - £114,000 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance | Benefits | Hear from the team ✨

⭐ Our Design team

We’re a team of 115+ designers, researchers and brand experts led by Chief Design Officer Vuokko Aro. We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.

Our brand helps make Monzo recognisable and human, whether someone is opening the app, visiting our website or seeing a campaign for the first time. As we grow, there’s a big opportunity to evolve how our brand shows up and make those experiences feel connected.

We’re looking for a Staff Brand Designer to help shape the future of Monzo’s visual identity, lead and develop designers, and set a high bar for creative work across the company.

You’ll join our digital-first internal creative studio and work closely with our Global Creative Director, designers and writers. You’ll also partner with teams across Product Design and Marketing, as well as external agencies, to bring ambitious ideas to life.

This is for a designer who loves getting into the detail as much as shaping the bigger picture and helping others grow. You’ll bring strong conceptual thinking, art direction and typography to your work, and support a team of designers to do their best work too.

🔑 You’ll play a key role by…

• Shaping our creative direction. Work with the Global Creative Director and partners across Monzo to evolve our visual identity and set a clear strategic direction for how the brand shows up globally.

• Leading ambitious work. You’ll lead projects from idea to delivery and oversee work led by others, helping the team solve problems and deliver their best work. You’ll spot opportunities, create briefs and bring the right people together to make ideas happen. You’ll thrive working across multiple projects and teams at once.

• Creating standout design. You’ll lead by example, setting a high bar for craft, concept and execution across the team. You’ll bring ideas to life across campaigns, marketing, product and other brand touch points, inspiring others through the quality of your work.

• Managing and developing designers. Lead and support a small team of designers, helping them grow through regular feedback, coaching and career development conversations. Use Monzo’s levelling frameworks to support their progression and set clear expectations.

• Raising the bar across the team. Lead critiques, share thoughtful feedback and mentor designers beyond your direct reports. Help create the conditions for people to do their best work.

• Connecting brand and product. Partner with Product Design teams to bring Monzo’s brand to life in the app, including developing visual concepts, art direction and motion storyboards for customer experiences.

• Evolving our brand systems. Develop guidelines, design principles and reusable assets that help teams create consistent, distinctive work as Monzo grows.

• Influencing decisions across teams. Bring people together around a creative vision, explain the thinking behind your work and navigate trade-offs between customer needs, creative ambition and business goals.

• Working with creative partners. Collaborate with external agencies and specialists, providing clear direction and feedback to make sure their work feels right for Monzo.

• Improving how we work. Spot opportunities to make our creative process more effective, whether that’s through new tools, better ways of working or clearer guidance for teams.

🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…

• You have a strong portfolio of brand design and campaign work, showing how you’ve developed distinctive creative ideas and brought them to life across different channels.

• You’re an expert in your craft, with particular strength in typography, visual identity and art direction . You care about the details and can show how they make the overall work stronger.

• You have experience managing and developing designers , including giving feedback, supporting career growth and helping people do their best work.

• You’ve led complex creative projects from brief to delivery, making decisions, bringing people with you and maintaining a high standard throughout.

• You can think beyond a single project: you’ve helped shape a brand’s direction, developed design systems or guidelines, or improved how creative work happens across a team or organisation.

• You’re comfortable working with ambiguity. You can define a direction, navigate competing priorities and make thoughtful trade-offs without losing sight of the bigger picture.

• You’re proactive, creating your own briefs, bringing the right people together to accomplish your goals. You’re not just a doer, but a problem solver and a self-starter.

• You enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, working across multiple teams and projects at the same time.

• You’re a confident collaborator who can explain and advocate for your ideas with designers, cross-functional partners and senior stakeholders.

• You enjoy raising the quality of design beyond your own work, through mentoring, critique and sharing what you know.

• You’re highly proficient in Figma and comfortable using the tools you need to develop and deliver your ideas. You have a clear interest in AI tools and are keen to explore and use them to evolve how we work and what we create across design, marketing and product.

• You have experience working in a digital-first brand, creative agency or in-house team, and can show how your work has supported customer or business goals.

• You can develop ideas for motion and communicate them through storyboards or creative direction. You don’t need to be a motion specialist.

We’d also love to see experience across areas such as web design, campaigns, print, film, illustration or 3D. You don’t need to be an expert in all of them.

🙌 What’s in it for you

💰 £98,000 - £114,000 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance.

⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team.

📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.

➕ Plus lots more! Take a look at our benefits .

• 30-minute call with our Recruiter

• 1-hour craft interview where you’ll present a single case study to 2 members of our Brand Design team.

• 1-hour interview covering values & ways of working.

To be considered for this role you will need to include your CV and a portfolio showcasing your work. This will allow us to better understand your experience. We’d particularly love to see projects you’ve led from start to finish, including the thinking behind the work, the impact it had and your individual contribution.

• Vous déplacer ponctuellement chez les clients pour des ateliers, des sessions techniques et pour développer la relation

• Au moins 5 ans d’expérience dans des fonctions techniques en contact avec les clients, comme Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer ou Technical Account Manager

• L’expérience de la conception d’architectures cloud évolutives et de l’intégration aux systèmes d’entreprise

• De l’aisance avec Python

• Une bonne connaissance des frameworks et outils LLM courants, ou un parcours en machine learning ou en data science

• Le goût de transmettre, d’accompagner et d’aider les autres à réussir

🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts , accounts for 16-17 year olds , a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save , invest and combine their pensions with us.

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not only about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo.

📍London | 💰£56,100 - £64,000 ➕ Incentive Awards tied to your performance ➕ Benefits | Hear from the team ✨

⭐ Our Regulatory team

We are looking for a curious, adaptive and data-focused Senior Regulatory Reporting Analyst with a strong attention to detail to join our regulatory reporting team at Monzo. The team is responsible for understanding our prudential regulatory reporting requirements, working on projects and submissions relating to these and collaborating with teams across Monzo.

🔑 You’ll play a key role by…

• Taking ownership of the preparation, analysis and submission of regulatory reporting requirements (e.g. Capital, Liquidity)

• Ensuring compliance with the applicable regulatory interpretations

• Assisting the wider team in producing Monzo’s capital and liquidity regulatory reporting and disclosures (including Pillar 3)

• Executing and improving the controls required to ensure regulatory reporting is timely, accurate and complete

• Ensuring high data quality by performing data profiling and investigating data quality issues

• Using data visualisation tools to build dashboards and facilitate sign-off and useful insights

• Partnering with teams internally to help them make informed business decisions and providing input into new product launches

• Designing brilliant ways to automate your work and leverage technology to ensure we scale with the business

🤩We’d love to hear from you if…

• You have a good understanding of capital requirements, liquidity reports and regulatory frameworks

• You’re excited by data and have a sharp eye for detail

• You have knowledge of coding languages (SQL would be a bonus), although a willingness to learn is just fine

• You have strong analytical skills, high attention to detail and the ability to meet tight deadlines

• You want to automate or enhance recurring processes, particularly by leveraging technology, and implement changes in collaboration with IT and regulatory change teams.

🙌 What’s in it for you

💰 £56,100 - £64,000 ➕ Incentive Awards tied to your performance

📍 This role is based in our London office, with a hybrid working approach

⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team.

📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.

➕ Plus lots more! Read our full list of benefits .

🌈 The application journey has 4 key steps:

• Phone call with recruiter

• Initial call with hiring manager (30 mins)

• Technical interview with hiring manager and team member (45 mins)

• Monzo behavioural interview (45 min)

This process should take around 3 - 4 weeks - your schedule is really important to us, so we promise to be as flexible as possible!

We’ll only close this role once we have enough applications for the next stage. Please submit your application as soon as possible to make sure you don’t miss out.

Anthropic is investing $50 billion in American computing infrastructure, including datacenters custom-built for our workloads, and this role sits at the heart of that effort. As a Staff Engineer on the Datacenter Server Lifecycle team, you will own the end-to-end operational journey of every machine in our datacenters – from initial provisioning and deployment, steady-state operation, maintenance, and repair.

This is greenfield work: you will help define the services, tooling, standards and processes that govern how we operate critical hardware at scale, powering frontier model development and serving. You will have the opportunity to define AI-native workflows for datacenter operations and to help drive innovations on efficiency, performance, and reliability.

A distinguishing aspect of this role is its deep intersection with security. The machines in our datacenter handle some of the most sensitive workloads in AI – training frontier models and serving millions of users interacting with Claude. Ensuring that every machine in the fleet is trusted, attested, and operating with a verified chain of integrity from the hardware up is a core part of the job, not an afterthought. You will partner closely with our Infrastructure Security team to define and enforce trusted compute standards across the lifecycle, from secure provisioning through end-of-life handling.

Key responsibilities

• Build automation to support datacenter fleets at scale.

• Define and own the end-to-end system lifecycle strategy – from provisioning and deployment through operation, maintenance, refresh, and decommissioning – and maintain automation and operational procedures for common lifecycle events (e.g., hardware failures, firmware upgrades, fleet rotations).

• Partner closely with Infrastructure Security to design and enforce trusted compute standards across the server lifecycle.

• Work closely with our Networking team to ensure end-to-end connectivity across all sites.

• Build and maintain tooling to track machine health, configuration, and operational status across the full datacenter fleet.

Minimum qualifications

• Hands-on experience with server hardware, including rack deployment, cabling, troubleshooting, and understanding failure modes at scale.

• End-to-end understanding of hardware lifecycle management: asset tracking, provisioning workflows, maintenance scheduling, and decommissioning practices.

• Proficiency in at least one programming language (e.g., Python, Rust, Go, or Java).

• Working knowledge of modern cloud infrastructure, including Kubernetes and large scale cloud providers (e.g. AWS, Azure, GCP).

• Ability to communicate clearly and build consensus with a wide range of stakeholders.

• Comfort navigating ambiguity and making progress on complex, cross-functional problems.

• Willingness to travel occasionally to datacenter sites across North America.

Preferred qualifications

• 8+ years of experience in datacenter infrastructure management, or a closely related discipline.

• Hands-on experience with GPU or AI accelerator hardware (e.g., NVIDIA A100/H100, Google TPUs, or AWS Trainium) and an understanding of their operational demands.

• Familiarity with modern provisioning and OS tooling such as LinuxBoot and NixOS

• Experience building or contributing to datacenter automation or fleet management platforms.

• Experience building and deploying server operating system distributions across large server fleets.

• Background in large-scale capacity planning and hardware refresh strategy, ideally at a hyperscaler or large cloud provider.

• Experience with trusted compute and hardware security concepts such as secure boot, TPM, hardware attestation, and firmware verification — or a strong desire to develop deep expertise in this area.

body:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Our team builds, tests, deploys, and monitors the classifiers that block internal agents from taking dangerous actions. These classifiers run across RL, evals, and internal deployments, and are designed to catch things like sandbox escape attempts or exfiltration of sensitive data.

When a classifier flags an action, it can block the action before the tool call runs, end the task, and alert a human . This is one layer of a defence-in-depth with several layers that reinforce each other: what our classifiers flag feeds into offline monitoring, and the findings from that go back into better classifiers and safer environment design.

The work combines research and production engineering:

•
The research problem is building high recall and high precision classifiers to catch rare, novel, and sometimes adversarial behaviour. There are also several narrow research questions to answer - for example, how to deploy safety classifiers inside training environments without incentivising models to evade them. Some research also builds on the multi-stage designs described in our work on Claude Code auto mode and Constitutional Classifiers .

•
The engineering problem is shipping these classifiers into the critical path of research and product work. These classifiers need to cover a huge volume of traffic while operating within cost, latency and availability constraints.

Day to day, much of our work is done with Claude: you'll direct agents to run experiments and ship code, and review what they produce. That moves the hard part of the job towards deciding what to do and in what order. Additionally, organisation, communication, and prioritisation skills matter a great deal as our classifiers sit in the path of many other teams' work.

Key responsibilities

•
Design, train, and evaluate classifiers that detect unsafe agent actions in real time, owning pieces such as prompted models, trained classifiers, or probes on model internals

•
Deploy, tune and operate these classifiers in the critical path of internal agents, RL training, and evaluations, and own their accuracy, reliability, latency, cost, and failure behaviour

•
Build the datasets, labelling pipelines, and evaluations that allow us to measure and improve our classifiers and harm taxonomies

•
Partner with red teaming colleagues to stress-test our classifiers, and harden them against what they find

•
Work with the teams whose agents, environments, and evaluations we run on, so that false positives get fixed quickly without weakening protection

•
Contribute to the team's direction, including what to build, what to partner on, and where to invest

Minimum qualifications

•
Ability to organise and prioritise several parallel streams of work, and to communicate clearly with the teams that work affects

•
Ability to critically review code and experiment results, including work produced by AI agents

•
Sincere interest in developing safe and beneficial AI systems

Preferred qualifications

•
Experience leading ambiguous technical projects and setting direction for other engineers or researchers

•
Experience evaluating large language models, developing classifiers, or operating high-scale production systems where requirements change quickly

•
Experience building detection systems where true positives are rare and false positives are costly, such as abuse, fraud, spam, or intrusion detection

•
Experience running low-latency, high-availability services that other systems depend on, including being on call for them

•
Experience fine-tuning language models, or working with probes and other methods that read model internals

•

•
Background in security, such as sandboxing or detection and response

•
Familiarity with research on AI control, scalable oversight, agent safety, or reinforcement learning

We’ve started building a sales team and testing a more personal approach. Now we’re looking for a Sales Manager to lead a team of Account Executives and help us turn what we’re learning into a repeatable, effective sales motion.

This is a chance to build something new. You’ll coach your team, help them deliver great results and use what you see every day to make the way we sell better. You’ll work closely with Revenue Operations (RevOps), Product and other teams to improve our processes and customer journeys.

You’ll also help build an AI-first sales motion from the start. We want someone who’s curious about AI and automation, actively experiments with new tools and can help the team spend more time on conversations that matter.

• Coaching and developing your team. Spend time listening to calls, reviewing opportunities and giving clear, regular feedback. Help each person build their skills and confidence, recognise great work and address underperformance fairly. Help hire and onboard new team members as we grow.

• Building the sales motion. Turn what you and your team learn into better ways of working. Spot friction in lead handling, follow-up, handovers and the sales process; test improvements, measure their impact and share what works so we can build a repeatable playbook.

• Staying close to customers. We expect Sales Managers to also take a few sales calls each week and make a few sales a month. Use what you learn from customers and the sales journey to coach the team, identify product needs and improve the motion. Most of your time will be spent leading the team and improving how we work.

• Putting AI and automation to work. Experiment with tools, agents and workflows that help the team research prospects, prepare for conversations, follow up or learn from calls. Work with specialist teams to test ideas responsibly, understand their impact and help the team adopt what works.

• Making good decisions with data. Use pipeline, conversion, activation, productivity and quality data to understand where the team is doing well and where customers or opportunities are getting stuck. Keep the pipeline accurate and work with RevOps on reporting and forecasting.

• Working as one team. Bring frontline insight to RevOps, Product, Marketing and Operations. Help shape the tools, processes and customer journeys Sales needs, and work together to solve problems that affect your team and customers.

• You work well with people in different teams. You can explain what your team and customers need, share evidence and help colleagues find solutions together.

• You care about doing the right thing for customers. You’re comfortable working within clear standards and learning what it takes to sell in a regulated environment.

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts , accounts for 16-17 year olds , a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save , invest and combine their pensions with us.

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not only about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo.

📍London | 💰£133,900 - £175,000 + equity + Incentive Awards tied to your performance + Benefits ✨

Our Monzo Business team ⭐

Monzo Business helps businesses manage their money, and more than +1 million businesses in the UK bank with us. Now, we’re exploring how we can help more established businesses switch to Monzo, across the UK and Europe.

Many of those businesses have more complex needs. They may need help understanding whether Monzo is right for them, moving their banking, or getting the most from our products. A great conversation with the right person can make a real difference.

We’ve started building a sales team and testing a more personal approach. We’re looking for someone to take those early learnings and build a repeatable, effective sales-led growth function for small and medium-sized businesses.

This is a chance to build something new. You’ll help shape which customers we serve, where a human conversation adds the most value, and how Sales works alongside self-serve, Product, Marketing and Operations. You’ll build the team and the playbook—and stay close enough to the work to test, learn and change direction yourself.

You’ll also have the opportunity to build an AI-native sales function from the start. We want someone who can rethink how the team finds, understands and serves customers: using AI and automation to remove work, improve decisions and give people more time for conversations that matter. That means experimenting, measuring what changes, and helping the team adopt better ways of working as the technology evolves.

🔑 You’ll play a key role by...

• Lead Sales for Monzo Business globally . You’ll define our sales strategy, build and lead the team, and be accountable for its performance and commercial impact. That means reaching and winning the right customers, improving conversion and productivity, and building a sales motion that can grow sustainably.

• You’ll work closely with RevOps, Product and other teams to help shape the targets, insights, tools and customer journeys Sales needs, and use them to guide decisions and improve results.

• Build the SMB sales motion . Turn what we’re learning from our pilot into a clear strategy for the businesses we can serve best. Test how inbound, outbound and self-serve journeys work together, and identify where a sales conversation makes a meaningful difference.

• Design the system around the customer . Work with RevOps, Marketing, Partnerships and Operations on targeting, lead generation, routing, sales process, reporting and forecasting. Spot where the journey breaks down and bring people together to fix it.

• Make Sales and Product ‘One Team’ . Share what you learn from customers and the sales funnel with Product, and work together on the experience, capabilities and product signals that help the right businesses discover and get value from Monzo.

Identify and test opportunities to redesign how the team works—from finding and prioritising prospects to preparing for conversations, following up, coaching and forecasting. Work with specialist teams to put useful tools and workflows in place, measure their impact and embed the ones that work.
